title: First Chicago jobs: Al Wynn, the Bookstore, Huey Swift
summary: Punch lists his first Chicago bands: Al Wynn at the Dreamland, a four-piece at the Bookstore, then Huey Swift at the Jeffery Club.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, that gives us a rough idea. Yeah. Now let's see. When you first got to Chicago, what was the first band you played with, other than Miramakas?
Well, the first band I played with was with, I see Al Wynn, he had a little band at the Dreamland.
Uh-huh. At the Dreamland, huh? Who was in the band?
Well, I don't know, me and Cliff Jones on drums, and some other guys, I can't remember them fellas now. Been a good while, you know.
Was this the same band that made the recordings?

No, no. Every time they make recordings, it's a couple of different bands, you know. One place I worked, I never did get to tell you, where I was doing very good, a place they called it the Bookstore, on 35th Street. It would open say twelve o'clock at night, and catch all the performance from all nightclubs and things, see. They called it the Bookstore, but they sold, you know, whisking stuff and things like that. But they did sell books in the front, and we had a little four piece outfit in there, and we just did good every night, every night. Had a lady on the piano, Ted Williams' wife, Irene her name was, and she the one supposed to have the little outfit, see. Well that's the time that Junior Cobb's come heard me play, and he's working out of South Chicago and Jeff with Huey Swift. And he come and heard me play that night, and I went back and told Huey about it, so Huey, he come on back and heard me play, and wanted me to join that big band out there.
What was the name of the club that Huey Swift was in?
It was the Jeffery Club, South Chicago and Jeffery.
I see. Now, you were first with Al when, and then with who?
I went to the bookstore, I told you. The bookstore? Yeah. And then Huey Swift? Yeah. That's right.
I got it, I see. And how long were you with Al when? Well I say a little more than a year or something. And how long were you with Irene Wilson, I guess her name was?

Yeah, Irene Wilson. Well we stayed at the bookstore about a couple of years, you know. Couple of years. Yeah. And I went with Huey Swift out there and worked over there three or four years, but the federal people closed that place. I don't know what was wrong, something was wrong there. And they closed it up, let's close it completely up. So that's the time I went with this Francois Louisianans.
